sections.content: You know the *pretérito indefinido* from A2 Unit 11 (and its contrast with the imperfect from A2 Unit 22). Here you use it to give a memory its turning point: something happened once, was witnessed, or was tried for the first time.

items.spanish: Por primera vez, me atreví a intervenir en el debate del auditorio.
items.english: For the first time, I dared to speak up in the debate in the auditorium.

items.spanish: Presencié una ceremonia intensa y la actuación terminó con un aplauso largo.
items.english: I witnessed an intense ceremony and the performance ended with long applause.

items.spanish: Aunque estaba nervioso, defendí a mi amiga delante de todos.
items.english: Although I was nervous, I defended my friend in front of everyone.

items.spanish: Cuando subí al escenario, el público guardaba silencio y me miraba.
items.english: When I went on stage, the audience was silent and looking at me.

sections.content: Choose the *indefinido* when the listener can locate the experience as one completed episode, even if its effect lasts. The *imperfecto* stays for the background (*estaba nervioso*, *guardaba silencio*).

sections.topic: the preterite for completed past events
